title: Emrys and the Will
premise: When the coffin of town founder Augustus Emrys is found empty during a ceremonial reburial, podcaster Vesper Delacroix realizes the town's founding legend is a cover story—and her three years of archived interviews contain the key to a witness everyone believes died decades ago. As the trial of Emrys's surviving heirs approaches, Vesper must decode her own recordings while dodging threats from people she's come to trust, discovering that her own arrival in town was never coincidence: she is the witness's granddaughter, placed in Hollow Creek by a dying woman's design. The witness, alive and hidden in plain sight as the courthouse archivist, finally testifies, and Vesper chooses to stay—not as an invisible outsider, but as the town's reluctant keeper of the truth.
about_author: Mara Vane is a former court stenographer from the Pacific Northwest who spent a decade transcribing small-town trials before turning to fiction. Her work explores how communities bury their pasts—and what it costs to dig them up.

chapters.title: The Empty Coffin
chapters.summary: Vesper covers the ceremonial exhumation of founder Augustus Emrys, expecting a routine bicentennial story. When the coffin lid opens to reveal nothing but century-old satin, the crowd's stunned silence tells her more than any official statement. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the thrill of a story colliding with the dread that her quiet, invisible life in Hollow Creek is over.

chapters.title: Three Years of Alphabetized Secrets
chapters.summary: Vesper retreats to her archive, reviewing three years of podcast interviews, convinced someone in them knew the coffin would be empty. She notices the town council's odd urgency to rebury quickly. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the comfort of her meticulous system cracking as she realizes the files hold a pattern she never looked for.

chapters.title: The Heirs of Augustus
chapters.summary: Vesper profiles the Emrys heirs—charismatic councilman Daniel and his brittle sister Margot—who announce a defamation suit against a local historian. Their grief reads as choreography. POV: Vesper, with a flashback transcript from Daniel. Emotional beat: unease as charm curdles into threat.

chapters.title: What the Gravedigger Buried Twice
chapters.summary: Vesper interviews elderly gravedigger Hollis, who hints that Augustus was buried twice—once in secret, decades before the official interment. He clams up when his grandson enters the room. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the loneliness of being the only one asking questions.

chapters.title: A Voice on the Tape
chapters.summary: Re-editing episode twelve, Vesper finds a background voice in her courthouse interview—a woman humming a lullaby Vesper inexplicably knows. Chilled, she realizes the song is one she's hummed her whole life without knowing its origin. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the first crack in her own identity.

chapters.title: The Archivist's Quiet Room
chapters.summary: Vesper visits the courthouse basement to pull land records and meets Ruth Calloway, the archivist who has worked there forty years. Ruth is kind, guarded, and strangely interested in where Vesper grew up. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: an odd, unplaceable warmth she can't explain.

chapters.title: Dead Men's Signatures
chapters.summary: Vesper discovers the founding charter bears a second signature—Elena Voss, a woman erased from every official history. The historian facing the defamation suit is the only person who ever wrote about her. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: righteous anger at how completely a person can be deleted.

chapters.title: Someone Is in the Archive
chapters.summary: Vesper's home studio is ransacked—nothing stolen, but her episode files are reordered, her alphabet broken. She understands it as a message: we know what you know. POV: Vesper, with a brief interlude in an unknown watcher's voice. Emotional beat: fear replacing the safety of routine.

chapters.title: The Historian's Confession
chapters.summary: The accused historian, Ada Reyes, tells Vesper that Elena Voss witnessed a killing in 1974—Augustus Emrys murdered his business partner, and Elena fled rather than testify. Ada believes Elena died in the mountains. POV: Ada, framed as a recorded interview. Emotional beat: grief for a woman history refused to save.

chapters.title: Trial Date Set
chapters.summary: The heirs' suit is scheduled, and the judge—whose family fortunes trace to Emrys money—refuses to delay. Vesper realizes any evidence must surface before opening arguments. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the clock becoming a physical weight.

chapters.title: Hollis Talks
chapters.summary: Hollis, frightened by the break-in, finally confesses: as a boy he helped rebury a second coffin under the Emrys mausoleum, and he saw Elena Voss alive years later, working in the county records office. POV: Hollis. Emotional beat: the relief and terror of an old man setting down a lifelong secret.

chapters.title: The Lullaby's Origin
chapters.summary: Vesper traces the lullaby to a songbook Ruth Calloway donated to the library in 1979. The connection snags in her chest: Ruth was in the records office. Ruth knew Elena. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: suspicion warring with the inexplicable tenderness she feels toward Ruth.

chapters.title: Margot's Warning
chapters.summary: Margot Emrys privately begs Vesper to stop, revealing she's terrified of her brother, not loyal to him—and that Daniel knows what's in the mausoleum. POV: Margot. Emotional beat: the tragedy of complicity and a woman trying, too late, to be brave.

chapters.title: Under the Mausoleum
chapters.summary: Vesper and Hollis's grandson open the mausoleum's false floor and find the second coffin—containing not Augustus, but his business partner's remains, hidden to bury the murder. Photographs are taken before Daniel's men arrive and chase them off. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: triumph instantly curdling into hunted panic.

chapters.title: Burned
chapters.summary: Daniel's lawyers get a court order sealing the mausoleum; Vesper's cloud backups are wiped; her landlord evicts her. The town she thought had accepted her closes like a fist. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the desolation of losing belonging just when she needs it most.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Filed Herself Away
chapters.summary: Vesper confronts Ruth with the lullaby and the records-office connection. Ruth admits she is Elena Voss—alive, hidden in plain sight for fifty years, too afraid to testify. Then Ruth reveals the second truth: she is Vesper's grandmother, and she arranged Vesper's move to Hollow Creek. POV: Ruth, then Vesper. Emotional beat: the ground giving way—identity, family, and purpose collapsing into one revelation.

chapters.title: Why Me
chapters.summary: Ruth explains: dying of heart failure, she needed someone unconnected, stubborn, and honest to finish what she couldn't. She chose her own granddaughter, then watched her for three years without ever saying a word. Vesper's fury and grief pour out. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: betrayal braided with the fierce, unwelcome love of finally belonging to someone.

chapters.title: The Choice to Testify
chapters.summary: Ruth agrees to testify, but only if Vesper publishes everything first—her podcast, the photos, the charter—so the truth can't be sealed again. They spend one long night assembling the final episode together. POV: alternating Vesper and Ruth. Emotional beat: two hidden women choosing, at last, to be seen.

chapters.title: Episode Fifty-Two: The Founding Lie
chapters.summary: The episode drops at dawn and detonates: national coverage, the judge recused under pressure, Daniel's donors fleeing. Daniel confronts Vesper on the courthouse steps with a threat that becomes a public confession when he realizes the microphones are live. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the exhale of a held breath three years long.

chapters.title: The Witness in Court
chapters.summary: Elena Voss—Ruth Calloway—takes the stand in the reopened criminal inquiry, identifying the 1974 killing and the burial of the partner's body. Her testimony cracks the heirs' case wide open; Daniel is charged. POV: Ruth. Emotional beat: fifty years of silence ending in a steady, unbroken voice.

chapters.title: What We Bury, What We Keep
chapters.summary: Augustus's coffin is reburied—this time with the partner's remains returned to his family and a new plaque naming Elena Voss in the founding record. Margot publicly disavows her brother. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: the quiet ache of a town learning to hold its whole history.

chapters.title: Keeper of the Record
chapters.summary: Months later, Vesper records a new season—not about secrets, but about how towns survive their truths. Ruth teaches her the archive; Vesper finally unpacks the boxes she never opened. POV: Vesper. Emotional beat: belonging no longer as something granted, but something chosen and kept.
